accounting: Sequential retries after a failed initialization can still overwrite prior owning globals. Source-positioned history records those old references as abandoned/unreleased allocations, separately from active authority. No VM-cleanup observation proves their reclamation.
finding: Ordinary Python loader reentry from a pathlib attribute callback can execute nested native initialization and change owning class globals during an SDK operation. An unconditional private-C-global frame across that operation was not justified before the source guard.

probe.kind: Bounded benign isolated CPython callback/loader probe; no engine invocation, VM or workload

result.kind: bounded isolated native initialization callback; no engine or VM

repair.behavior: The public initializer wraps the unchanged private body with an active guard and a permanent-success guard. Nested and later successful-image initializer calls fail before the body; failures permit later sequential retries. Ordinary cached imports remain usable.
repair.evidenceScope: The root-owned source guard structure/layout and actual source replay are checked; full actual callback-frame composition is still required. Tests alone are not a source guarantee.

status: Concrete finding preserved; source guard implementation/current replay exists; complete module/callback and public-caller integration remains active.
